sentences.text:
Appellant :- Saddam
Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Appellant :- Manvendra Singh
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Sharad Kumar Srivastava

Hon'ble Surendra Singh-I,J.
Heard Sri Manvendra Singh, learned counsel for the appellant, Sri Sunil Kumar Tripathi, learned A.G.A. for the State, Sri Sharad Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the respondent no. 2 and perused the record.
The present criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed against the order dated 20.09.2022 passed by Special Judge, (S.C./S/.T. Act)/ Additional Sessions Judge, Fatehpur, whereby the learned Judge has rejected the Bail Application No. 1927 of 2022 (Saddam Vs. State of U.P.) moved on behalf of the appellant in Case Crime No. 79 of 2022 under Sections 376, 323, 504, 506, 452 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)5, 3(2)5a, 3(1)? & 3(1)? of S.C./S.T. (P.A.) Act, Police Station- Dhata, District- Fatehpur.
According to prosecution case, on 10.06.2022, at 2 a.m., the appellant-accused entered and reached on terrace of informant's house where she was sleeping with her two children.
The appellant-accused put a knife on her neck, threatened her to kill her and forcibly carried her into the room and after putting her on the ground, committed rape on her.

It has been submitted on behalf of the appellant that :-

sentences.text: (iv) the appellant is in jail since 11.06.2022 and has criminal history of 4 cases explained in paragraph no. 22 of the affidavit filed in support of the bail application.
In case he is enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent no. 2 and learned A.G.A. for the State have opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.
They have submitted that the informant/victim supported the prosecution case in her statements recorded u/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
They next submitted that in the medical examination of the informant/victim, injuries were found on the neck and eye.
They have further submitted that informant's daughter, eye-witness Gunja Devi and her uncle, Brijesh Raidas has supported the prosecution case.

Considering the submissions made on behalf of the learned counsel for the appellant, learned A.G.A.
and learned counsel for the respondent no. 2, facts and circumstances of the case, medical report of the informant/victim, statement of the witnesses u/s 161 Cr.P.C. and that of the victim u/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., statements of P.W.1 informant/victim and P.W.2 Gunja Devi recorded in the court during trial but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the appellant-accused at this stage.

Accordingly, the appeal is disposed of with the direction to trial court to conclude the trial of the case as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of one year from the date of filing of certified copy of this order before the court concerned, if there is no legal impediment.
The observations made in this order is only for the purpose of bail and it shall not impact the proceedings of the trial court while deciding the case on merits.
